PHP

Deep Learning — Beginner to Advanced v8.4 Server-side 75+ Practice Q's

Complete PHP learning path from syntax fundamentals to advanced concepts. Each section includes theory, code examples, and practice questions to test your understanding. Covers PHP 8.0 through 8.4 features.

PHP Basics

Syntax & Variables

PHP code is embedded in HTML using <?php ... ?> tags. Variables start with $ and are loosely typed.

<?php
$name = "Alice";
$age = 25;
$price = 19.99;
$isActive = true;

// Variable variables
$varName = "greeting";
$$varName = "Hello"; // $greeting = "Hello"

// Constants
define("SITE_NAME", "MyApp");
const VERSION = "1.0";

// Data types
var_dump($name);   // string(5) "Alice"
echo PHP_VERSION; // 8.4.x
Type System
TypeExampleDescription
string"hello"Sequence of characters
int42Whole numbers
float3.14Floating point numbers
booltrueBoolean value
array[1, 2, 3]Ordered map
objectnew stdClass()Class instance
nullnullNo value
resourcefopen(...)External resource

PHP 8.x: mixed, never, void, union types (int|string), intersection types (Countable&Stringable), true/false as standalone types.

Operators
// Arithmetic
$sum = 10 + 5;  // 15
$pow = 2 ** 8;  // 256 (exponentiation)

// Comparison
var_dump(5 == "5");   // true  (loose)
var_dump(5 === "5");  // false (strict)
var_dump(5 <=> 3);     // 1    (spaceship)

// Null coalescing
$username = $_GET['user'] ?? 'guest';

// Null coalescing assignment (PHP 7.4+)
$data['key'] ??= 'default';

// Match expression (PHP 8.0)
$result = match($status) {
    200 => 'OK',
    404 => 'Not Found',
    500 => 'Server Error',
    default => 'Unknown',
};

Control Flow

Conditionals & Loops
// if / elseif / else
$score = 85;
if ($score >= 90) {
    echo "A";
} elseif ($score >= 75) {
    echo "B";
} else {
    echo "C";
}

// Switch
switch ($day) {
    case "Mon": echo "Work"; break;
    case "Sat":
    case "Sun": echo "Weekend"; break;
    default: echo "Unknown";
}

// Match (PHP 8.0) - strict ===, returns value
$status = match($code) {
    1, 2, 3 => "low",
    4, 5, 6 => "medium",
    7, 8, 9 => "high",
    default => "unknown",
};

// Loops
for ($i = 0; $i < 5; $i++) { echo $i; }

foreach ($items as $key => $value) {
    echo "$key: $value";
}

while (condition) { /* ... */ }
do { /* runs at least once */ } while (condition);

// Alternative syntax for templates
foreach ($users as $user): end?>
    <li><?= $user['name'] ?></li>
<?php endforeach;

Arrays

Indexed & Associative Arrays
// Indexed array (short syntax)
$colors = ["red", "green", "blue"];
$colors[] = "yellow"; // append

// Associative array
$user = [
    "name" => "Alice",
    "role" => "admin",
    "skills" => ["PHP", "JS"],
];

// Array destructuring (PHP 7.1+)
[$a, $b, $c] = $colors;
['name' => $name, 'role' => $role] = $user;

// Spread (PHP 7.4+)
$arr1 = [1, 2];
$arr2 = [3, ...$arr1, 4]; // [3, 1, 2, 4]
Key Array Functions
FunctionDescriptionExample
array_map()Apply callback to each elementarray_map(fn($n) => $n * 2, $nums)
array_filter()Filter elementsarray_filter($nums, fn($n) => $n > 0)
array_reduce()Reduce to single valuearray_reduce($nums, fn($c, $n) => $c + $n, 0)
array_merge()Merge arraysarray_merge($arr1, $arr2)
array_column()Extract column from 2Darray_column($users, 'name')
array_search()Search value, return keyarray_search('red', $colors)
in_array()Check if value existsin_array('php', $tags)
array_unique()Remove duplicatesarray_unique($items)
array_chunk()Split into chunksarray_chunk($items, 3)
array_walk()Modify in placearray_walk($arr, fn(&$v) => $v .= '!')

String Functions

Essential Functions & Examples
// Length & case
$text = "Hello PHP World";
echo strlen($text);           // 16
echo strtoupper($text);       // "HELLO PHP WORLD"
echo ucwords($text);          // "Hello PHP World"

// Search (PHP 8.0+)
var_dump(str_contains($text, "PHP"));    // true
var_dump(str_starts_with($text, "Hello")); // true
var_dump(str_ends_with($text, "World"));   // true

// Position & extract
$pos  = strpos($text, "PHP");  // 6
echo substr($text, 0, 5);              // "Hello"
echo str_replace("World", "Laravel", $text); // "Hello PHP Laravel"

// Split & join
$parts = explode(" ", $text);     // ["Hello", "PHP", "World"]
echo implode("-", $parts);       // "Hello-PHP-World"

// Format & cleanup
echo trim("  spaced  ");                     // "spaced"
echo htmlspecialchars("<b>bold</b>");   // "<b>bold</b>"
echo sprintf("Hello %s, ID: %04d", "Alice", 7); // "Hello Alice, ID: 0007"
String Functions Reference Table

All functions require PHP 4.0+ unless marked with a version badge (e.g. 8.0).

FunctionDescriptionUse Case
strlen()Get byte lengthInput length validation
str_contains() 8.0Check if haystack contains needleSearch filters, keyword detection
str_starts_with() 8.0Check string prefixURL routing, protocol check
str_ends_with() 8.0Check string suffixFile extension validation
strpos()Find first occurrence positionExtract after delimiter
substr()Extract substring by positionTruncate text, get initials
str_replace()Replace all occurrencesTemplate vars, sanitization
explode()Split string by delimiterCSV parsing, tag splitting
implode()Join array into stringBuild SQL lists, format output
trim()Strip whitespace from endsInput sanitization
strtolower()Convert to lowercaseCase-insensitive comparison
strtoupper()Convert to uppercaseNormalize codes
ucfirst()Capitalize first characterName formatting
ucwords()Capitalize each wordTitle case
sprintf()Format with placeholdersError messages, DB queries
str_pad()Pad string to lengthFormat IDs, align output
str_repeat()Repeat string N timesSeparators, padding
str_word_count()Count wordsReading time estimate
nl2br()Newlines to <br>Render user text in HTML
strip_tags()Remove HTML/PHP tagsSanitize rich text
Leading Tips & Real-World Use Cases
Tip 1: Prefer str_contains() over strpos()
str_contains($haystack, $needle) (PHP 8.0+) returns a boolean â€” clearer intent, no risk of misinterpreting strpos() === 0 vs === false.
Tip 2: Use mb_* for UTF-8 safety
strlen() counts bytes, not characters. Use mb_strlen(), mb_substr(), mb_strpos() for multi-byte encodings (emoji, CJK, accented chars).
Tip 3: explode() + list() for parsing
list($name, $email) = explode(',', $line); â€” clean one-liner for CSV lines, config pairs, or delimiter-split data.
Tip 4: sprintf() for templates
sprintf('Hello %s, your ID is %04d', $name, $id); â€” cleaner than concatenation with built-in formatting.
Tip 5: URL & file checks with str_starts_with/str_ends_with
str_starts_with($url, 'https://') for protocol; str_ends_with($file, '.pdf') for extension â€” readable and fast.
Tip 6: Trim all user input
$input = trim($_POST['email']); â€” users paste extra whitespace. Combine with filter_var() for robust validation.

Functions

User-defined & Arrow Functions
// Named function with typed parameters
function greet(string $name, string $prefix = "Hello"): string {
    return "$prefix, $name!";
}

// Strict types (declare at file top)
declare(strict_types = 1);

// Variadic arguments
function sum(int ...$numbers): int {
    return array_sum($numbers);
}

// Named arguments (PHP 8.0)
greet(prefix: "Hi", name: "Bob");

// Arrow functions (PHP 7.4+)
$double = fn($n) => $n * 2;

// Closures
$greeter = function (string $name) use ($prefix) {
    return "$prefix $name";
};
Variable Scope & Static
$global = 10;

function test() {
    global $global;  // access global
    static $count = 0; // persists across calls
    $count++;
    return $count;
}

// Anonymous classes
$obj = new class("value") {
    public function __construct(public string $prop) {}
};

Object-Oriented Programming

Classes & Constructor Promotion
class User
{
    // Promoted constructor properties (PHP 8.0)
    public function __construct(
        private string $name,
        public string $email,
        protected int $age = 0,
    ) {}

    public function getName(): string {
        return $this->name;
    }

    public function setName(string $name): static {
        $this->name = $name;
        return $this; // fluent interface
    }
}

$user = new User("Alice", "alice@test.com", 30);
echo $user->email; // public property
Inheritance, Interfaces & Traits
interface Notifiable
{
    public function notify(string $message): void;
}

trait Loggable
{
    public function log(string $msg): void {
        echo "[LOG] $msg";
    }
}

class Admin extends User implements Notifiable
{
    use Loggable;

    public function notify(string $message): void {
        $this->log("Sending: $message");
    }

    // Covariant return type
    public function setName(string $name): static {
        return parent::setName("Admin: $name");
    }
}

Advanced OOP

Abstract, Final, Readonly & Magic Methods
// Abstract class
abstract class Shape
{
    abstract public function area(): float;
}

final class Circle extends Shape
{
    public function __construct(
        private readonly float $radius
    ) {}

    public function area(): float {
        return pi() * $this->radius ** 2;
    }
}

// Magic methods
class Config
{
    private array $data = [];
    public function __get(string $key): mixed {
        return $this->data[$key] ?? null;
    }
    public function __set(string $key, mixed $value): void {
        $this->data[$key] = $value;
    }
    public function __toString(): string {
        return json_encode($this->data);
    }
}
Namespaces & Autoloading
// File: src/Http/Request.php
namespace App\Http;

class Request
{
    public function method(): string {
        return $_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'];
    }
}

// Usage
use App\Http\Request;
use App\Http\Request as HttpRequest;

$req = new Request();

// composer.json PSR-4 autoloading
// "autoload": { "psr-4": { "App\\": "src/" } }
require 'vendor/autoload.php';

File Handling & Error Handling

// File read/write
$content = file_get_contents('data.txt');
file_put_contents('output.txt', "Hello", FILE_APPEND);

// CSV parsing
$rows = array_map(fn($line) => str_getcsv($line), file('data.csv'));

// Error handling
try {
    throw new RuntimeException("Something broke");
} catch (RuntimeException $e) {
    error_log($e->getMessage());
} finally {
    echo "Always runs";
}

// Custom exception
class ValidationException extends InvalidArgumentException {}

// Multiple catch (PHP 7.1+)
catch (RuntimeException|LogicException $e) {}

Forms, Sessions & Cookies

session_start();

// Session data
$_SESSION['user_id'] = 42;
$userId = $_SESSION['user_id'] ?? null;

// Cookie
setcookie('theme', 'dark', time() + 86400*30, '/', '', true, true);

// Form handling
if ($_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] === 'POST') {
    $name = htmlspecialchars($_POST['name'] ?? '', ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8');
    $email = filter_input(INPUT_POST, 'email', FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL);
}

// File upload
if ($_FILES['avatar']['error'] === UPLOAD_ERR_OK) {
    move_uploaded_file($_FILES['avatar']['tmp_name'], 'uploads/avatar.jpg');
}

MySQL & PDO

PDO Connection & Prepared Statements
$dsn = "mysql:host=localhost;dbname=test;charset=utf8mb4";
$pdo = new PDO($dsn, "root", "", [
    PDO::ATTR_ERRMODE => PDO::ERRMODE_EXCEPTION,
    PDO::ATTR_DEFAULT_FETCH_MODE => PDO::FETCH_ASSOC,
    PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES => false,
]);

// Prepared statement
$stmt = $pdo->prepare("SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = :email");
$stmt->execute(['email' => $email]);
$user = $stmt->fetch();

// Insert + return ID
$pdo->prepare("INSERT INTO users (name) VALUES (:name)")->execute(['name' => $name]);
$id = $pdo->lastInsertId();

// Transaction
$pdo->beginTransaction();
try {
    /* multiple queries */
    $pdo->commit();
} catch (PDOException $e) {
    $pdo->rollBack();
}
PDO Fetch Modes
ModeDescription
FETCH_ASSOCColumn-name-indexed array
FETCH_NUMColumn-number-indexed array
FETCH_BOTHBoth (default)
FETCH_OBJAnonymous object
FETCH_CLASSInto a class instance
FETCH_KEY_PAIRFirst col as key, second as value
FETCH_GROUPGroup by first column

Security

// 1. XSS Prevention
echo htmlspecialchars($input, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8');

// 2. SQL Injection - use prepared statements
$stmt = $pdo->prepare("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ?");
$stmt->execute([$id]);

// 3. Password hashing
$hash = password_hash($password, PASSWORD_BCRYPT, ['cost' => 12]);
if (password_verify($input, $hash)) { }

// 4. CSRF token
$_SESSION['csrf'] = bin2hex(random_bytes(32));

// 5. Input validation
$email = filter_var($_POST['email'], FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL);
$age = filter_var($_POST['age'], FILTER_VALIDATE_INT, ['options' => ['min_range' => 1, 'max_range' => 120]]);

// 6. Secure session settings
ini_set('session.cookie_httponly', 1);
ini_set('session.cookie_secure', 1);
ini_set('session.use_strict_mode', 1);

Data Structures & Algorithms

// Stack (array)
$stack = [];
array_push($stack, 'a');
$top = array_pop($stack);

// Queue (SplQueue)
$queue = new SplQueue();
$queue->enqueue('a');
$front = $queue->dequeue();

// Two Sum
function twoSum(array $nums, int $target): array {
    $map = [];
    foreach ($nums as $i => $num) {
        $diff = $target - $num;
        if (isset($map[$diff])) return [$map[$diff], $i];
        $map[$num] = $i;
    }
    return [];
}

// Binary search
function binarySearch(array $arr, int $target): int {
    $left = 0; $right = count($arr) - 1;
    while ($left <= $right) {
        $mid = intdiv($left + $right, 2);
        if ($arr[$mid] === $target) return $mid;
        if ($arr[$mid] < $target) $left = $mid + 1;
        else $right = $mid - 1;
    }
    return -1;
}

// Fibonacci (DP)
function fib(int $n): int {
    $dp = [0, 1];
    for ($i = 2; $i <= $n; $i++)
        $dp[$i] = $dp[$i-1] + $dp[$i-2];
    return $dp[$n];
}

Design Patterns

// Singleton
final class Database
{
    private static ?Database $instance = null;
    private function __construct() {}
    public static function getInstance(): Database {
        return self::$instance ??= new self();
    }
}

// Factory
class LoggerFactory
{
    public static function create(string $type): Logger {
        return match($type) {
            'file' => new FileLogger,
            'db' => new DbLogger,
            'cloud' => new CloudLogger,
        };
    }
}

// Repository
interface UserRepository {
    public function findById(int $id): ?User;
    public function save(User $user): void;
}

Dependency Injection & PHPUnit
// Dependency Injection
class UserService
{
    public function __construct(
        private UserRepository $users,
        private MailerInterface $mailer,
    ) {}
}

// PHPUnit test
class UserServiceTest extends TestCase
{
    public function testRegisterSendsEmail(): void
    {
        $repo = $this->createMock(UserRepository::class);
        $mailer = $this->createMock(MailerInterface::class);
        $service = new UserService($repo, $mailer);
        $result = $service->register('test@test.com');
        $this->assertTrue($result);
    }
}

Practice Questions

75+ questions covering every topic. Click to reveal the answer.

1PHP Basics

Variables, types, operators, syntax.

echo can output multiple strings separated by commas and is slightly faster. print returns 1 and can be used in expressions. Both are language constructs.

isset() checks if a variable is declared and not null. empty() returns true for "", 0, "0", null, false, [], or unset variables.

== coerces types before comparing ("5" == 5 is true). === checks value and type ("5" === 5 is false). PHP 8.0+ made comparisons stricter (no longer treats 0 == "abc" as true).

define("NAME", value) runs at runtime and can be used anywhere. const NAME = value is compile-time and can be used inside classes. const is slightly faster. PHP 8.3 allows const with dynamic expressions.

8 types: string, int, float, bool, array, object, null, resource. PHP 8.2 added true/false as standalone types. Union types (int|string) and intersection types (Countable&Stringable) are also supported.

$x = $a ?? $b ?? 'default' returns first non-null. $data['key'] ??= 'default' (PHP 7.4+) assigns only if null. Both replace lengthy ternary + isset() patterns.

2Control Flow

Conditionals, loops, match.

foreach: iterate arrays/objects. for: known iteration count. while: unknown iterations, condition at start. do-while: guarantees at least one iteration.

match uses strict (===), returns a value, supports multiple conditions per arm (1, 2 => 'x'), throws UnhandledMatchError if no match. switch uses loose comparison, needs break, doesn't return a value.

Returns -1, 0, or 1. Used in usort callbacks: usort($arr, fn($a, $b) => $a <=> $b). Works with strings, numbers, arrays, and objects.

Uses : instead of { with endif/endfor/endforeach/endwhile. Useful in templates: <?php foreach($items as $item): ?> ... <?php endforeach; ?>

3Arrays

Indexed, associative, functions, spread.

array_unshift($arr, $v) / $arr[] = $v (or array_push) for adding. array_shift() / array_pop() for removing.

array_map applies callback, returns new array. array_filter filters by truthy callback. array_reduce reduces to single value. All are immutable.

Extracts a column from a 2D array. array_column($users, 'name') returns ['Alice', 'Bob']. Third param sets key column: array_column($users, 'name', 'id').

Unpacks arrays: $arr = [1, ...$middle, 4]. Works with Traversable objects (PHP 8.1+). Supports string keys (PHP 8.1+). Also used in function calls to unpack argument arrays.

array_key_exists('key', $arr) checks key existence (even if value is null). isset($arr['key']) returns false if value is null. Use array_key_exists when null vs missing matters.

4Strings

String manipulation, searching, formatting, tips.

str_contains($haystack, $needle) (PHP 8.0+) returns a boolean â€” cleaner for existence checks. strpos() returns the integer position or false if not found â€” requires strict !== false check. Always prefer str_contains() when you only need a yes/no answer.

trim($str) removes whitespace from both ends. ltrim()/rtrim() for left/right only. Critical for sanitizing user input â€” emails, usernames, and file paths often have accidental spaces from copy-paste.

function isSecure(string $url): bool {
    return str_starts_with($url, 'https://');
}
str_starts_with() (PHP 8.0+) is the most readable. Pre-8.0: strpos($url, 'https://') === 0. Also useful for file extensions (str_ends_with($file, '.pdf')).

Use mb_* functions: mb_strlen(), mb_substr(), mb_strpos(), mb_strtolower(). Set internal encoding: mb_internal_encoding('UTF-8'). strlen() counts bytes â€” a single emoji or CJK character can be 3-4 bytes, causing bugs in truncation and validation.

function isPalindrome(string $str): bool {
    $cleaned = preg_replace('/[^a-z0-9]/', '', strtolower($str));
    return $cleaned === strrev($cleaned);
}
Strips non-alphanumeric chars, lowercases, then compares with strrev(). Works for "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama". For multibyte: use mb_strtolower() and mb_strrev() (roll your own via preg_split()).

5Functions

User-defined, arrow, closures, scope.

Functions are standalone callables. Methods are functions inside a class with access to $this and visibility modifiers (public/private/protected).

Pass by parameter name: func(name: 'Alice', age: 30). Skip optional params. Named must come after positional. Breaks BC if param names change.

Arrow functions (fn($x) => $x*2) are single-expression, auto-capture by value. Closures use function + use() syntax, support multiple statements, can capture by reference (&$var).

Local, global, static scope. Globals need "global $var" or $GLOBALS['var'] inside functions. "static $count" persists between calls. Superglobals ($_GET, $_POST, etc.) are always accessible.

function factorial(int $n): int {
    return $n <= 1 ? 1 : $n * factorial($n - 1);
}
No, PHP does not optimize tail recursion. Deep recursion (>10k depth) causes stack overflow. Use iteration or trampolines.

6Object-Oriented Programming

Classes, inheritance, interfaces, traits, magic methods.

Define and initialize properties directly in the constructor: __construct(private string $name, public int $age). Eliminates separate property declarations.

Abstract classes can have implementations + properties; extends one only. Interfaces define contracts; implement many. PHP 8+ allows interface constants and abstract private methods.

Traits are reusable code blocks used via "use Loggable, Timestampable;". They solve the diamond problem, support abstract methods and properties. Conflict resolution via insteadof/as.

__construct (instantiation), __destruct (cleanup), __get/__set (dynamic props), __call/__callStatic (dynamic methods), __toString (string conversion), __invoke (callable object), __clone (deep copy), __debugInfo (var_dump), __serialize/__unserialize (PHP 7.4+).

Covariance: subclass method returns more specific type (Admin vs User). Contravariance: subclass method accepts less specific parameter (Animal vs Dog). Supported in PHP 7.4+.

7Advanced OOP

Namespaces, autoloading, readonly, anonymous classes.

Declared with "namespace App\Http;". Use via "use App\Http\Request;" or FQCN "\App\Http\Request". Support aliasing: "use ... as HttpRequest". Prevents name collisions.

PSR-4 maps namespace prefixes to directories. "App\\": "src/" means App\Http\Request loads from src/Http/Request.php. Composer generates vendor/autoload.php. Run "composer dump-autoload" to regenerate.

readonly properties (PHP 8.1) set once in constructor. readonly classes (PHP 8.2) make all properties readonly implicitly. Great for DTOs. Cannot combine with static or untyped properties.

PHP's generic empty class. Used when casting arrays to objects: (object) ['name' => 'Alice'] or json_decode() without the second argument.

For one-off implementations: new class extends Logger { ... }. Useful in tests (mocks), callbacks, or when a full class definition is overkill. Supports constructors and inheritance.

8MySQL & PDO

PDO, prepared statements, transactions.

PDO provides a consistent interface for MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, etc. Supports prepared statements, named parameters, transactions, and multiple fetch modes. Safer and more portable than mysqli.

Query and data are sent separately. SQL template is compiled first; parameters are bound as data only. Even malicious input cannot alter query structure. Set PDO::ATTR_EMULATE_PREPARES to false for real prepared statements.

beginTransaction() â†’ execute queries â†’ commit()/rollBack(). Wrap in try/catch. Nested transactions not natively supported (use savepoints).

FETCH_ASSOC (column names), FETCH_NUM (numbered), FETCH_BOTH, FETCH_OBJ (object), FETCH_CLASS (class instance), FETCH_KEY_PAIR (key-value), FETCH_GROUP (grouped). Use ASSOC for general, CLASS for ORM.

Use JOINs or WHERE id IN (...) to batch-load relations. E.g., SELECT u.*, p.* FROM users u LEFT JOIN posts p ON p.user_id = u.id WHERE u.id IN (:ids).

9Security

XSS, SQL injection, CSRF, hashing.

Escape output with htmlspecialchars($data, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8'). Use template engines that auto-escape. Set Content-Type header, X-Content-Type-Options, and CSP headers.

password_hash($pwd, PASSWORD_BCRYPT) creates 60-char hash with random salt. PASSWORD_ARGON2ID (PHP 7.3+) is more secure. Use password_verify() to check. Adjust cost: BCrypt=12, Argon2: memory=1024K.

CSRF tricks users into unwanted actions. Mitigate with: CSRF tokens in forms (bin2hex(random_bytes(32))), SameSite=Lax cookie attribute, custom AJAX headers, Origin/Referer checking.

function handleUpload(array $file): string {
    $allowed = ['image/jpeg', 'image/png'];
    $ext = pathinfo($file['name'], PATHINFO_EXTENSION);
    if (!in_array($file['type'], $allowed) || !in_array($ext, ['jpg','png']))
        throw new RuntimeException('Invalid');
    $name = bin2hex(random_bytes(16)).'.'.$ext;
    move_uploaded_file($file['tmp_name'], 'uploads/'.$name);
    return $name;
}
Never trust $_FILES['type']. Validate MIME with finfo, regenerate filenames.

Validates and sanitizes input: FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL, FILTER_VALIDATE_URL, FILTER_VALIDATE_INT with min/max range, FILTER_SANITIZE_EMAIL, etc. Use for all external input.

12Data Structures & Algorithms

Stacks, queues, sorting, searching, DP.

function binarySearch(array $arr, int $target): int {
    $l = 0; $r = count($arr) - 1;
    while ($l <= $r) {
        $mid = intdiv($l + $r, 2);
        if ($arr[$mid] === $target) return $mid;
        if ($arr[$mid] < $target) $l = $mid + 1;
        else $r = $mid - 1;
    }
    return -1;
}

function twoSum(array $nums, int $target): array {
    $map = [];
    foreach ($nums as $i => $num) {
        $diff = $target - $num;
        if (isset($map[$diff])) return [$map[$diff], $i];
        $map[$num] = $i;
    }
    return [];
}
O(n) time complexity.

function fib(int $n): int {
    $dp = [0, 1];
    for ($i = 2; $i <= $n; $i++)
        $dp[$i] = $dp[$i-1] + $dp[$i-2];
    return $dp[$n];
}
O(n) time, O(n) space. Can optimize to O(1) space with two variables.

O(1) amortized. PHP arrays are hashtables internally. array_push (or $arr[] =) appends to the end with amortized O(1). array_unshift is O(n) because it reindexes.

class LoggerFactory {

Centralizes object creation, allows easy extension.

Abstracts data access logic behind an interface. Controllers don't know about PDO/ORM â€” they call $repo->findById(). Swappable implementations (MySQL, Redis, in-memory). Testable with mocks.

DI: dependencies passed via constructor (explicit, testable). Service Locator: dependencies requested from a container inside the class (hidden coupling). DI is preferred â€” follows Inversion of Control.

Strategy pattern allows runtime algorithm swapping without modification. Each strategy is a separate class implementing an interface. Better than switch when algorithms are complex, need testing in isolation, or need dynamic selection.

14SOLID & Advanced

SOLID, PHPUnit, static analysis, async.

Single Responsibility Principle â€” a class should have one reason to change. Makes code easier to understand, test, and maintain. If a class does too much, split it into separate classes.

Open/Closed: open for extension, closed for modification. Example: instead of modifying a PaymentProcessor to add PayPal, create a PayPalPayment implements PaymentMethod. Add new methods without changing existing code.

Liskov Substitution: subtypes should replace their base types without breaking behavior. Violation: Square extends Rectangle â€” setting width on a Square also changes height, breaking Rectangle expectations.

Use a framework (Laravel/Symfony). Structure: src/ (PSR-4), tests/, public/, config/, routes/. Follow SOLID, use DI, repositories, services, and value objects. Automated CI with PHPUnit, PHPStan, PHP-CS-Fixer.

PHP-FPM handles concurrent requests via process pool. For high concurrency: use OPcache, async processing (Queues + workers), read replicas, connection pooling, HTTP caching (Varnish/CDN), horizontal scaling (multiple servers behind load balancer). Consider Swoole/ReactPHP for long-running async apps.
